summary: A first-person action passage from Book 6, part 36, in which the narrator, caught in an attack, swats a thrown firebomb-style bottle back at its attackers, which explodes against the van and sets men aflame. The narrator's sleeve catches fire, and the narrator rolls under the van and shoots the surviving attackers in the legs, aiming for arteries. The narrator counts the dead, ten so far, and wonders whether more attackers remain.
one_line: In Book 6, part 36, the narrator deflects a bottle of napalm back at attackers, then shoots survivors in the legs amid the fire.
key_facts: The narrator swings an arm down and around and strikes a flaming bottle with the heel of the hand, sending it back the way it came.
The flame from the bottle blisters the narrator's hand, and the narrator's sleeve catches fire.
The narrator smothers the burning sleeve by smashing it against the body while ducking.
The narrator calculates the bottle's fall using the math of free fall, solving for time when the height is zero.
The bottle's explosion is too loud for the narrator to hear it shatter.
The napalm splatters against the van's metal, and the flames lick up above the van's roof.
The narrator rolls under the van and retrieves a Colt pistol.
The narrator shoots the surviving attackers in the legs, aiming for the arteries rather than to wound.
The narrator has counted six burning bodies on the ground and shot three more.
The narrator's count of the dead totals ten, including one killed earlier in the SUV.
The narrator wonders whether the attackers would really have sent more than twelve men.
The narrator suspects the remaining attackers may be trying to stop their friends from bleeding out or burning, or have their sights set on the van.

entities.name: Colt
entities.role: handgun the narrator retrieves from the ground and uses to shoot the attackers

entities.name: SUV
entities.role: vehicle in which the narrator previously killed one attacker, counted in the total of ten
